# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to establish communication first since this is the first turn. I can see the bomb but can't hear anything, so Mute won't hear me anyway (Mute can't hear speech either, wait - let me check reach). Actually Mute "cannot speak or touch" but can Mute hear? Let me check my own channels: I can speak to Mute and Blind, and gesture to Mute only (since Blind can't see gestures).

I should report what I see. Blind can hear my speech (Blind can hear, just can't see or touch). Mute cannot hear anything either per the rules ("Mute: cannot speak"... but hearing isn't restricted for Mute explicitly - wait, checking table: Mute "Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb" - hearing isn't listed as forbidden, so Mute CAN hear). Let me re ­check Blind: "Cannot: See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed" - so Blind can hear.

So both Mute and Blind can hear my speech. I'll report the display, light, and wires clearly.

```
speak(text="Display shows the number 3. Light is white. There are five wires in order: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute gestured one symbol to me - "☝" (index finger up). Since I can see gestures, this likely means Mute is pointing to something - possibly indicating "wire 1" or "item 1" or asking about a specific numbered thing. Since Mute has the manual, they might be trying to signal which wire/item corresponds to a rule, but a single gesture with no prior established code is ambiguous. I have no way to know what Mute intends without an established convention, and Mute cannot speak to explain gestures to me only received by Mute anyway (gestures reach Mute already, this is confusing - wait, Mute gestured TO me, meaning I received it since I can see).

So Mute sent gesture ☝ to me. This is likely them referencing "1" - maybe asking about wire 1, or confirming display digit relates to something. Without established protocol, I should acknowledge and try to build a shared reference. Let me speak to both, restating info and referencing "1" to see if that aligns.

Since I can't hear Mute's clarification (Mute cannot speak), Mute must always communicate via gesture to me. I should try to interpret ☝ as "one" / "first" and respond by confirming numbered facts so Mute can correlate.

```
speak(text="Confirming again: display 3, light white, wires in order are 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange. If you mean wire number 1, that wire is white.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]

Mute gestured 👍 ☝ to me — this looks like confirmation (👍 = yes/correct) plus ☝ (one/first) — likely confirming "yes, wire 1" as relevant, perhaps the manual says something about wire 1 specifically, or confirming my guess about wire 1 being important.

This suggests the manual instructs something regarding wire index 1, matching display "3"? Or maybe Mute is building a numbering system with me: 👍 = confirm/yes, ☝ = the number "1". They may want me to send numbered gestures back so they can correlate manual instructions to what I see.

Since Mute cannot speak, and needs to communicate rule details, they're likely using gestures with me to establish a shared code (thumbs up = yes, numbers via finger gestures) so I can relay confirmed facts to Blind (who can hear but not see).

I should try responding with gestures too, to confirm receipt, and also speak the wire colors again for Blind's benefit, and try to build a yes/no gesture protocol with Mute.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
speak(text="For Blind: wires in order are 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange. Display shows 3, light is white. Mute, I confirmed wire 1 is white if that's what you're asking.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]

Mute repeated the same gesture 👍 ☝ again. Since gestures aren't heard and Mute can't speak, Mute is likely confirming/repeating because they didn't get feedback loop closure, or this is their way of establishing "yes = 👍" and "wire/step 1 = ☝" firmly, waiting for me to act on it or pass to Blind.

Given the order is Mute → Blind → Deaf each round, my message this round only reaches players next round. Blind won't get my speech until they can act on it. Let me think about the turn order: Mute speaks/gestures first, then Blind, then Deaf (me). What I send now lands on whoever comes after me in this round — but I'm last, so my messages land at the start of next round for Mute and Blind.

Mute keeps gesturing "👍 ☝" identically twice — since I already acknowledged, perhaps this is Mute's actual instruction meaning something like "cut wire 1" (👍=do it/confirm action, ☝=wire one), intended to reach Blind eventually. But gestures I make only reach Mute (Blind can't see gestures). So Mute is telling *me* something, expecting me to relay it as speech to Blind since Blind can hear but not see.

That makes sense! Mute can't speak to Blind directly. Mute gestures to me, I translate/relay via speech to Blind. So 👍☝ likely means "cut wire 1" or "wire 1 is correct/safe".

I should relay this to Blind as speech.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute is signaling about wire 1 - repeated the same gesture twice, likely meaning wire 1 is the one to act on, possibly cut wire 1.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]

Mute keeps sending the exact same gesture again — 👍 ☝ — for the third time now. This repetition despite my relay suggests either:

1. Mute hasn't received my speech yet (turn order: Mute speaks before Blind and Deaf each round, so Mute only sees what I sent in the *next* round after I send it — my turn 4 message should have reached Mute by their turn 5 already, but Mute's action this round was already decided before seeing it, since Mute goes first).

2. Mute is stuck repeating because they don't have gesture-receiving capability from me confirmed, or they're waiting for something else - like waiting for Blind to act and confirm.

Actually - key realization: Mute speaks first each round. So the gesture I see from Mute in "Turn N" was sent in response to what Mute saw at start of round N (i.e., from Blind's turn in round N-1, since Mute doesn't hear my speech until round N+1 relative to when I send it... let me not overthink). 

The repetition is consistent - Mute is confirming wire 1 repeatedly, likely because that's genuinely the instruction and they're waiting for action/confirmation. I already relayed to Blind. Let me continue relaying and confirm to Mute I understand, using a distinct acknowledgment gesture combo to signal "understood, told Blind."

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute continues signaling the same thing: wire 1. This strongly suggests wire 1 is the correct action - likely cut wire 1.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 1 was cut successfully — display changed from 3 to 6, and wire 1 shows [CUT]. Mute gestured 👍 👍 back to me, confirming acknowledgment/success of that action, matching my last gesture to them.

Now the bomb state has changed: display is 6, light still white, wires 2-5 remain (red, green, blue, orange). I need to report this new state to both Mute and Blind so we can figure out the next step. Since display changed to 6, this is a new clue for Mute to check against the manual.

```
speak(text="Wire 1 cut successfully. New state: display now shows 6, light still white. Remaining wires: 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝]

Mute gestured ✌ ☝ this time — different from before. Following the established pattern where numbers seem to be indicated by finger-count gestures (☝=1, ✌=2), this could mean "2 1" or perhaps "21" or refers to wire 2 first then something, or maybe it's indicating "wire 2" (✌) and then a confirmation digit (☝=1st action/step).

Given the previous pattern was 👍(yes/action)+☝(wire1), now it's ✌(2)+☝(1) — this could mean wire 2, or could mean "step/rule 21" or "second instruction, first part". Given consistency, most likely interpretation: ✌ = wire 2, ☝ = confirm/first priority, i.e., "cut wire 2 next."

I'll relay this to Blind as the likely next action, while flagging uncertainty since order of symbols differs from before.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute now signals wire 2 - gesture pattern changed from before but likely means: cut wire 2 next.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```
